title: Companion Lucas-Number Shallow-Diagonal Identities
description: Answers the parent's second open question: the companion Lucas-number diagonal identities and a mixed Fibonacci–Lucas identity. Mathlib has Fibonacci numbers but no Lucas sequence, so this entry introduces the Lucas numbers L(0)=2, L(1)=1, L(n+2)=L(n)+L(n+1) and proves (i) the bridge L(n)+F(n)=2·F(n+1), (ii) the Lucas–Fibonacci relation L(n+1)=F(n+2)+F(n), (iii) that L(n+2) is the sum of two consecutive shallow diagonals of Pascal's triangle (in both index conventions), reducing to the parent's fib_shallow_diagonal, and (iv) the mixed product identity F(2n)=F(n)·L(n) via Mathlib's Nat.fib_two_mul. Axiom-free.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: None. #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound for all five named results. No axiom declarations, no sorries, and no native_decide (the two base cases use decide on concrete fib values, which reduces in the kernel without ofReduceBool).
originalContributions: lucas: the Lucas sequence L(0)=2, L(1)=1, L(n+2)=L(n)+L(n+1), absent from Mathlib (which has only the unrelated Lucas–Lehmer primality test)
lucas_add_fib: the subtraction-free bridge L(n) + F(n) = 2·F(n+1)
lucas_eq: the Lucas–Fibonacci relation L(n+1) = F(n+2) + F(n)
lucas_shallow_diagonal: L(n+2) = ∑_j C(n+2−j, j) + ∑_j C(n−j, j), the companion Lucas diagonal identity (sum of two consecutive shallow diagonals of Pascal's triangle)
lucas_shallow_diagonal_alt: the mirror form L(n+2) = ∑_k C(k, n+2−k) + ∑_k C(k, n−k)
fib_two_mul_lucas: the mixed Fibonacci–Lucas product identity F(2n) = F(n)·L(n)

overview.historicalContext: The shallow (rising) diagonals of Pascal's triangle sum to the Fibonacci numbers; the parent entry (combinations-formula-oq-01-oq-01) proved this as ∑_j C(n−j, j) = F(n+1), axiom-free, and posed as its second open question the companion Lucas-number diagonal identities and the mixed Fibonacci–Lucas diagonal sums. The Lucas numbers L_n = φ^n + ψ^n are the second canonical solution of the Fibonacci recurrence (L_0=2, L_1=1), satisfying L_n = F_{n−1} + F_{n+1}. Mathlib formalizes F (Nat.fib) but not L, so a self-contained development is required.
overview.problemStatement: Introduce the Lucas numbers in Lean and express them through the shallow diagonals of Pascal's triangle, together with a mixed Fibonacci–Lucas identity, reusing the parent's Fibonacci diagonal sum.
overview.text: We define lucas by the two-step recurrence and prove the subtraction-free bridge L(n) + F(n) = 2·F(n+1) by two-step induction (Nat.twoStepInduction), the inductive step matching the Lucas and Fibonacci recurrences term by term. From the bridge and Nat.fib_add_two we read off the Lucas–Fibonacci relation L(n+1) = F(n+2) + F(n). For the diagonal identities we use L(n+2) = F(n+3) + F(n+1) and replace each Fibonacci number by its shallow-diagonal sum (the parent's fib_shallow_diagonal and its mirror form, replicated here so the file is self-contained), giving L(n+2) as the sum of the (n+2)-nd and n-th shallow diagonals. Finally, Mathlib's Nat.fib_two_mul writes F(2n) = F(n)·(2·F(n+1) − F(n)); the bridge identifies the second factor as L(n), yielding F(2n) = F(n)·L(n).
overview.proofStrategy: Prove one subtraction-free bridge L+F=2F' by two-step induction; derive the Lucas–Fibonacci relation, the two diagonal identities (by reduction to the parent's Fibonacci diagonal sums), and the mixed product identity (from Nat.fib_two_mul) all from it, discharging natural-number arithmetic with omega.
keyInsights: Phrasing the Lucas–Fibonacci link as L(n)+F(n)=2·F(n+1) avoids natural-number subtraction entirely and makes a single two-step induction suffice for everything downstream.

A Lucas number is the sum of two consecutive shallow diagonals of Pascal's triangle, because L(n+2)=F(n+3)+F(n+1) and each Fibonacci number is one shallow diagonal — so the parent's identity is reused verbatim, twice.
The 'mixed' product identity F(2n)=F(n)·L(n) is exactly Mathlib's Nat.fib_two_mul once the bridge identifies 2·F(n+1)−F(n) as L(n).
prerequisites: Fibonacci numbers Nat.fib and the recurrence Nat.fib_add_two, the doubling identity Nat.fib_two_mul
The parent's shallow-diagonal Fibonacci identity ∑_j C(n−j, j) = F(n+1)

conclusion.summary: The companion Lucas-number diagonal identities are proved: after defining the Lucas sequence (absent from Mathlib), L(n+2) is shown to be the sum of two consecutive shallow diagonals of Pascal's triangle (both index conventions), the Lucas–Fibonacci relation L(n+1)=F(n+2)+F(n) is established, and the mixed identity F(2n)=F(n)·L(n) is derived from Nat.fib_two_mul. 10 theorems, 1 definition, 146 lines, axiom-free.
conclusion.implications: Resolves the parent's second open question and adds the first Lucas-number development to the gallery, with the Lucas sequence packaged for reuse (recurrence, Fibonacci bridge, doubling identity).
openQuestions: Prove the single-diagonal Lucas identity L_n = ∑_k (n/(n−k))·C(n−k, k) directly (the weighted form), rather than as a sum of two unweighted shallow diagonals.
Establish the Lucas analogue of Cassini's identity, L(n−1)·L(n+1) − L(n)² = (−1)^{n−1}·5, over ℤ.
